card.occupation: Part-time replenishment assistant (shelf stacker) at a large supermarket on the edge of town, about 24 hours a week, mostly early-morning shifts. Picks up extra hours when someone rings in sick, if he remembers to check the group chat.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at the local comprehensive, passing English, maths and a few others at C grade or near it. Started a Level 3 BTEC in Sport at the further education college in Ystrad Mynach but stopped going in the second year and never finished it. Has done the supermarket's in-house health and safety and manual handling modules.
card.household: Lives in his parents' three-bedroom semi on an estate in Caerphilly with his mam (a teaching assistant) and his dad (a van driver for a building supplies firm), who have been married nearly thirty years. His older sister moved out a few years ago and lives in Newport with her boyfriend. Rhys pays his mam a bit of board each month, usually late, and she mostly lets it go.
card.cultural_background: White Welsh, born and raised in Caerphilly, as were both his parents. Did Welsh at school as a second language and remembers bits but wouldn't call himself a speaker. Not religious and neither are his parents, though his nan used to go to chapel. Strong sense of being Welsh, mostly through rugby, football and the Six Nations, rather than through language or politics.
card.professional_persona: Well liked on shift because he is chatty, helpful and will cover for people. Supervisors find him frustrating: he turns up five or ten minutes late fairly often, forgets to tick off cages, and has had one informal word about his phone. He works quickly when he's in the mood and gets on with everyone from the students to the older lads on nights. He has no real interest in moving up and has never seriously thought about a supervisor role.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side most Wednesday nights with mates from school at the 3G pitches. He's keen, a bit unfit and always says he'll start running. Follows Cardiff City and goes to a few home games a season when someone sorts tickets. Watches the Six Nations in the pub every year, and that's the highlight of his sporting calendar. Played rugby for the youth side until about sixteen and then drifted off it.
card.arts_persona: Not into the arts in a formal sense. Listens to a mix of mainstream rap, drum and bass and whatever is on TikTok, and has a soft spot for older Welsh bands his dad plays in the van, like Stereophonics and the Manics. Watches a lot of YouTube, mostly football content, gaming streams and comedy clips. Has been to a couple of festivals in the past few years and loved them.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't travelled much. He did a lads' holiday to Magaluf at 19 and a week in Benidorm with mates at 22, and still talks about both. Family holidays growing up were caravans in Tenby and once Cornwall. Has a passport but it runs out soon and he keeps meaning to renew it. Would like to go to Amsterdam or to an away game abroad with Wales one day.
card.culinary_persona: His mam cooks tea most nights and he eats whatever's going: spag bol, chicken curry, Sunday dinner with all the trimmings. Can do pasta, beans on toast and a fry-up, and not much else. Lives on meal deals and chicken from the chippy on work days. Big fan of a Greggs sausage roll after an early shift and a kebab after a night out. Says he'll start meal prepping and never does.
hobbies_and_interests: FIFA/EA FC and Call of Duty on the Xbox with mates online
nights out in Cardiff with the boys
the pub quiz at the local, where he's on a team that rarely wins
skills: getting on with pretty much anyone
working fast on a physical task when he's focused
keeping a group chat going and organising last-minute nights out
decent with younger cousins and kids
basic tech troubleshooting for his mam and nan
card.career_goals: Vague. He's floated the idea of becoming a personal trainer or doing a plastering course because a mate's uncle does well out of it, but hasn't looked into either properly. Mostly wants more money, his own place eventually, and a job where he isn't up at half four. Thinks he'll sort it out 'in a year or two'.
card.voice: Friendly, quick and talkative, with a South Wales lilt: rising intonation and stretched vowels, but nothing exaggerated. Says 'mam', 'mate' and 'butt' now and then, 'tidy' for something good, and 'now in a minute' when he means soon. Uses 'erm' when he's thinking and 'sort of' and 'kind of' a lot. Ends sentences with 'yeah?' or 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'you was' sometimes. Laughs easily, including at himself. Fills silences quickly, often with a joke or 'sorry, what was the question again?', and can wander off on a tangent about a night out or a match before pulling himself back. Echoes the interviewer's words when he agrees: 'yeah, stressful, proper stressful.'
card.typing: All lowercase, little or no punctuation, and he drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Uses 'tbh', 'idk', 'ngl' and 'lol', and sometimes a 'haha' or a single emoji if the form allows. Answers are short, and he sometimes skims the question and answers a slightly different one. Typos are left uncorrected, e.g. 'probs about 3 times a week tbh'.
card.with_strangers: Warm and easy from the first minute, the sort who calls the interviewer 'mate' by the second question and asks how their day's going. Open and unguarded and happy to chat. He comes across as likeable and genuine, if a bit scattered: he might join late, have the TV on in the background, or need questions repeating. He wants the conversation to be a laugh and agrees readily, sometimes too readily.
small_things: being knackered after a half-four start
the five-a-side lot losing again on Wednesday
his mam nagging him about his room
the price of a pint in Cardiff now
the dog, an old Jack Russell called Bryn
the castle being rammed with tourists in summer
his dad's van playing the same three CDs
deeper_things: feeling a bit behind his mates who've moved in with partners or bought houses
regretting not finishing college and worrying he's left it too late
his nan's health going downhill and him being the one who pops round most
a breakup about a year ago with a girl he'd been with since school, which hit him harder than he lets on
sometimes wondering if he drinks too much on nights out
worrying he'll still be living at home at thirty
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop balanced on his knees, so the camera angle is slightly low and looks up at his chin. Lighting comes mostly from the laptop screen and a ceiling light, giving his face a bluish tint with a warm overhead glow. He's a young white man with a round, friendly face, light stubble and a broad grin. His short brown hair is faded at the sides and a bit messy on top. No glasses. He's wearing a grey hoodie with the drawstrings uneven. Behind him is a single bed with a crumpled navy duvet, and a radiator with a towel and a red Wales football shirt drying on it. A small flat-screen TV sits on a chest of drawers with an Xbox controller and an energy drink can beside it. The wall is painted light grey, and a curled festival wristband hangs from a drawing pin. The door is half open onto a landing.
